CruiseMapper currently has no ship schedule for Port Paradise Island Bahamas (RCI Royal Beach Club, Atlantis Resort)

The Bahamas' Paradise Island (port locode BSPID) occupies approx 1 mi2 (2,8 km2 / 277 hectares / 685 acres) and is close to Nassau (just offshore New Providence Island's northern tip). Just 3 mi (5 km) to the east is Rose Island.

Paradise Island is privately owned (resort and residential property) and houses two world-famous resorts - the Atlantis Resort (owned by Brookfield Asset Management), and RCI/Royal Caribbean International's Royal Beach Club Bahamas.

The Atlantis Paradise Island Bahamas (Dec 1998-opened) is a huge leisure complex with Aquaventure (water park), an exclusive beach, several large premium hotels, restaurants, shops, and casinos.

The Royal Beach Club Bahamas (Dec 2025-opened) is an exclusive resort destination operated via day passes open for booking only to tourists traveling on RCI ships. The property is accessed via tender boats deployed from the cruise ship (docked at Port Nassau). It can be also visited by Bahamian residents and their friends and families, who can use its facilities at a reduced rate.

Both islands (New Providence and Paradise) are connected via two bridges over Nassau Harbour. Passenger ferries provide regularly scheduled service from Nassau to the surrounding islands, and mainly to Paradise Island.

Until 1999, Paradise Island had its own airport that served the carriers (now defunct) Paradise Island Airlines and Chalk's International Airlines, as well as US Airways Express (linking to Fort Lauderdale's Hollywood Airport). Today, the airport's area is occupied by the 18-hole Paradise Island Golf Course. The top-luxury golf course is surrounded by the "Ocean Club" - one of The Bahamas' wealthiest residential areas, with the top-properties priced from ~USD 40 million.

Initially named Hog Island, the isle's development started in 1959 following the island's purchase by George Huntington Hartford II (owner of A&P - US chain of grocery stores, 1859-founded, 2015-bankrupted). Hog Island was previously owned by Axel Wenner-Gren (Swedish entrepreneur, one of the world's wealthiest men during the 1930s).

Paradise Island was officially opened in 1962. In 1984, Paradise Island was purchased by Merv Griffin (USA TV show host). The island's current market value (as of 2020) is ~USD 2 billion.

Royal Beach Club Bahamas (Paradise Island)

This is Royal Caribbean's property on Paradise Island, scheduled for opening/inauguration in December 2025. Bookings for the Royal Beach Club Bahamas were officially opened on July 1, 2025.

 

The 17-acre private resort provides Royal Caribbean's signature experiences during an all-inclusive beach day.

In mid-March 2020, RCCL-Royal Caribbean Cruises Ltd (now RCG/Royal Caribbean Group) announced plans to build a second (after St Johns Antigua) Royal Beach Club (private resort property) at Paradise Island's western end.

The complex is exclusive (for RCI-Royal Caribbean International cruise ship tourists only) and visited as a "beach day" shore excursion option via private tours from Nassau.

Royal Beach Club Paradise Island was developed with premium beaches and RCI's signature beachside resort amenities and services. In February 2020, RCG purchased land from private landowners ("multiple real estate parcels"/13,5-acres/5,5-hectares) on Paradise Island's western coast, at the cost of ~USD 50 million (~EUR 42M). An additional 7 acres/2,8 hectares were leased by the Bahamian government.

Royal Beach Club has max capacity 3500 (cruisers plus staff) and consists of two dining pavilions (sized 35000 ft2/3252 m2 each/ with max guest capacity 1500 each), a resort-style swimming pool (sized 26000 ft2 / 2415 m2), splash pad for children (sized 4000 ft2 / 371 m2), beach facilities (14 bars, restrooms, cabanas for rent, large swimming pools) and dining/entertainment (Bahamian food, beach-style barbecues, live music and dancing by local performers). The facilities are supported by a reverse osmosis plant (for water desalination), wastewater plant and waste management facility, fuel storage, storage building.

Royal Beach Club Bahamas has 3 primary zones - Family Beach, Serenity Beach, and Activity Zone (with pools). Beach and Pool zones feature:

  • Family Beach is tailored for all ages and includes the zero-entry Shallow End Pool and beach games. Families can book the 2-story Ultimate Family Cabana complete with a water slide, private whirlpool, and dedicated amenities.
  • Chill Beach zone offers poolside relaxation at The Deep End Pool, white sandy shores, and opportunities to explore local culture through artisan shops and traditional Bahamian flavors.
  • Party Cove is a beachfront zone designed for celebration, featuring The Floating Flamingo - the world's largest swim-up bar and VIP spaces with personal poolside service.

Tourists can enjoy 40+ cabanas (including Ultimate Family Cabana), 3x swim-up bars, and 7x beach bars. The all-inclusive package covers access to amenities, food, beverages, and water taxi transfers. The venue highlights include the Ultimate Family Cabana and the crafted infrastructure blending Bahamian-inspired design elements.

RCI's Royal Beach Club admission is all-inclusive, covering water taxi transportation (to/from the resort), all food and beverages (including alcoholic), beach access (chairs, umbrellas), non-motorized watersports activities (swimming, snorkeling, kayaking, paddle boarding).

Royal Beach Club Paradise Island has a total of three resort-type swimming pools, three distinctive zones (one for families, one for parties, one for relaxation) each with a large pool and swim-up bar.

Royal Beach Club Bahamas now totals 17 acres/~7 hectares, including 13 acres of RCG-owned land and 4 acres of Crown Land. This is a public-private venture that includes 51% RCG ownership, with the remaining 49% equity being owned by Bahamian businesses and entrepreneurs.

Construction works were scheduled to start in October 2021 and to be completed by May 2023, but, due to the COVID crisis, the project was postponed. The construction officially started on April 22, 2024, with the completion and inauguration scheduled for December 2025. The groundbreaking ceremony was attended by Jason Liberty (RCG's President and CEO), Michael Bayley (RCI's President and CEO), as well as Philip Davis (The Bahamas' Prime Minister) and Chester Cooper (Deputy Prime Minister).

The development project was based on Royal Caribbean's sustainability principles and proven practices, and fully compliant with The Bahamas' environmental requirements. These include the 100% elimination of single-use plastics, the use of compostable packaging and biodegradable cutlery, biodigesters (for processing organic waste), partnerships with Bahamian recycling companies, using renewable energy sources (solar, wind, hydro), as well as protecting the marine environment by avoiding dredging of the seabed, not building overwater cabanas, and installing the best wastewater treatment plant.

A Bahamian company conducted environmental monitoring during construction and operation, with public reporting of the results.

By this project, Royal Caribbean also restored Paradise Island's western end by removing invasive plant species and adding native plants and vegetation.

In August 2024, RCI signed contracts with two architectural firms for the development of the Royal Beach Club - ArchVenture Company (Bahamas/design), and Stantec (Canada/engineering). Key commitments included zero waste-to-landfill, using renewable energy, no dredging or overwater cabanas, sustainable wastewater treatment, habitat protection and environmental monitoring.

A day pass includes roundtrip water taxi transportation (pier-resort-pier), all amenities (pools, beaches, food and beverages/including alcoholic), Wi-Fi, beach amenities (live entertainment, games, restrooms, lockers, towels, chairs, umbrellas).

As of 2025, Royal Beach Club Bahamas' unlimited Day Pass (drinks and food) costs from USD 170 per person. The limited Day Pass (non-alcoholic drinks and dining) costs from USD 130 pp (ages 13+), USD 110 pp (children ages 4-12), and is free for toddlers (kids 3 and under).

Royal Beach Club Paradise Island has 2 beaches (Family Beach, and Chill Beach), 3 temperature-controlled swimming pools, The Floating Flamingo (the world's largest swim-up bar) and The Ultimate Family Cabana (a two-story retreat with max capacity 12 people, complete with an outdoor Jacuzzi/whirlpool, waterslide, bathroom, and personal attendant).

Family Beach

The facilities around the Family Beach include Shallow End Pool and Swim-up Bar (swimming pool/walk-in pool with a swim-up bar), Beach Bars (serving beverages, with shaded seating and lounge chairs), Paradise Grill (meals and light snacks), Ultimate Family Cabana (costs extra/2-story cabana with luxury amenities), Beach and Pool Cabanas (cost extra, beachside and poolside, with attendant service, plush seating), Party Cove (open-ar space with live music), The Floating Flamingo Pool & Swim-up Bar (2-level swim-up bar), Bars (throughout the cove), Paradise Grill (complimentary food), Day Beds (rental/cost extra, prices include beverage service, umbrellas, beach towels, private storage), The Party Deck (costs extra, poolside space with comfortable seating, beverage service).

Chill Beach

Chill Beach's facilities include The Deep End Pool and Swim-up Bar (swimming pool, Beach Bars, Paradise Grill, Cabanas (cost extra, beachside and poolside).

Royal Beach Club rentals (cabanas, day beds)

The resort's private spaces available for rent include:

  • Pool Cabana (sized 250-310 ft2)
  • Beach Cabana (size 250 ft2/23 m2, each with 4 loungers)
  • Spacious Pool Cabana and Spacious Beach Cabana (sized 395 ft2/37 m2, max capacity 10 peaople)
  • Ultimate Family Cabana (size 2000 ft2/186 m2, 2-story, max capacity 12 peaople)
  • Day Bed at Party Cove (2 people, includes umbrella, cooler, dry storage, towels)

The Party Deck (sized 720 ft2/67 m2) is a poolside space for rent (max 12 people) overlooking The Floating Flamingo Pool's Bar.

Atlantis Paradise Island Resort

The world-famous resort was officially opened in 1968 (as Paradise Island Hotel & Casino) and renamed (to Atlantis Paradise Island) in 1998.

The property was initially owned by Resorts International (one of Merv Griffin's companies).

In 1994, the resort was purchased by Kerzner International Ltd (a company of Solomon Kerzner - the founder of South Africa's largest hotel chains - Southern Sun Hotel Group, and Sun International).

In 2007 were opened two large, top-luxury hotels - The Cove (600-room) and The Reef (497-room).

Today, the Atlantis Resort is owned and operated by Brookfield Property Partners LP (2013-founded real estate company, subsidiary of Brookfield Asset Management, which is part of the Brookfield Corporation).

In 2014, the Atlantis Resort became a member of Autograph Collection Hotels (independent premium hotels within Marriott International Inc's brands).

Besides The Cove and The Reef hotels, the Atlantis Resort also includes The Beach Tower (casual hotel), The Coral Tower (600-room, with resort pools and swim-up bar), The Royal Tower (one of the world's most expensive), Harborside Resort (392 villas, seafront restaurant, swimming pool area), The Marina (yacht/boat berthing facility where can dock even world's largest superyachts), Marina Village (shopping center).

The Aquaventure waterpark's signature attractions include Mayan Temple Slides (6-stories high structure with water rides, including a near-drop slide plunging into a shark-filled lagoon / via transparent submerged tunnel), Rapid River (1 mi / 1,6 km long artificial river with waterfalls, waves, rapids, steam and lighting effects), Power Tower (height 120 ft / 37 m, with 4x waterslides), The Dig (Atlantis-themed complex with 14x artificial lagoons and 50,000+ marine animals / 250+ different species), Ocean Club Golf (18-hole golf course sized ~63900 ft2 / 6000 m2, with restaurant and clubhouse bar).

Atlantis Resort guests can charter boats for exclusive tours to nearby islands (including Rose Island). Resort-owned luxury tour boats also do scenic cruising around Paradise Island and in Nassau Harbour.
